metadata.title: Symmetry Transition Preserving Chirality in QCD: A Versatile Random Matrix Model

extraction_notes.note: Numbered equations (10) and (14) retyped from equation to claim: the text calls them 'the result' / 'a new result' and the conclusions present them as the paper's derived results.
Derivations are in running prose with no proof markers; each proof ends before the sentence that displays the derived formula, so the result is not nested in its own proof.
PRL letter with \paragraph headings only, no \section commands, so every node has an empty section; the key expansion steps are omitted and deferred to a companion paper.
Physics motivation (applications to lattice QCD, condensed matter), the measure/normalization remarks after (3), and the figure caption are not extracted as nodes.

nodes.statement: As we have already pointed out, an exact chirality yields for a complex matrix a linear level repulsion from the origin, though the range where this is happening is of order O(widehatmu) for small widehatmu.
conclusions: As we have already pointed out, an exact chirality yields for a complex matrix a linear level repulsion from the origin, though the range where this is happening is of order O(widehatmu) for small widehatmu.

nodes.statement: In we have shown that the spectral statistics describe a Pfaffian point process meaning that all k-point correlation functions as well as averages over ratios of characteristic polynomials of the random matrix D are given by Pfaffian determinants which only comprise three functions.
conclusions: In we have shown that the spectral statistics describe a Pfaffian point process meaning that all k-point correlation functions as well as averages over ratios of characteristic polynomials of the random matrix D are given by Pfaffian determinants which only comprise three functions.
nodes.raw_latex: In~\cite{Kanazawa:2018a} we have shown that the spectral statistics describe a Pfaffian point process meaning that all $k$-point correlation functions as well as averages over ratios of characteristic polynomials of the random matrix $\mathcal{D}$ are given by Pfaffian determinants which only comprise three functions.
